issues.body: `resolver_errexit` is only `"set -euo pipefail" in resolve_run`. A non-crashing mutant such as inserting `set +o pipefail` after the existing `set -euo pipefail` leaves this assertion and every behavioral resolver assertion green: the behavioral harness executes only the Python heredoc, not the surrounding shell pipeline. In the real workflow, a resolver refusal then becomes the left side of `python3 ... | tee`; without pipefail, `tee` can return zero, so the targets job succeeds while publishing no usable `repos` value. The assertion therefore does not prove the fail-closed behavior its name and comment claim.
issues.fix_hint: Test the shell control at the execution seam rather than by substring. Parse/pin the effective command sequence so no command can disable `errexit` or `pipefail` before the exact resolver pipeline, or execute the extracted run block in a controlled shell fixture and assert that a refusing resolver produces a nonzero step result. Add a non-crashing `set +o pipefail`-before-pipeline mutant and require the same named check count as pristine.
issues.title: Pipefail assertion passes when the resolver pipeline runs with pipefail disabled

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 2 closes the prior producer/dependency finding: the self-test now pins `backfill.needs`, the job-output binding, the resolver step identity and input binding, and executes the resolver against independent policy fixtures covering full sweep, narrowing, disabled/unknown targets, and an empty enabled set. However, the newly claimed pipefail guard remains a containment assertion and can stay green when pipefail is disabled before the resolver pipeline. That permits resolver refusal to be masked by `tee`, allowing the targets job to report success without a valid matrix output. Because this is a new major fail-closed gap in the added producer seam, changes are still required.
